input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='CLASSIFICATION.md'
s=open(p).read()
a=s.index('- [ ] **K8 — accuracy against the published numbers.**')
b=s.index('## Handoff')
new='''- [x] **K8 — accuracy against the published numbers** (2026-09-25).
  `cmd/kev -suite` runs one of Kev's frozen suites and scores it as
  `kev.benchmark` and `kev.metrics` do: argmax, Brier and ECE over the clean,
  knowable rows, raw Brier from the served p (p^T renormalised is
  softmax(z)), and the unknowable share at p ≥ 0.9. `-compare` pairs two row
  files. `reference/kev_suite_fp32.py` writes the same rows from Kev's own
  code in fp32 on the CPU (`model.probs`, ~1.3 s a transfer-v4 record, ~5 s a
  decision-v7 one; it resumes an interrupted file). The suites are copied
  from Kev's repo at `9fdf054` into `models/kev-suites/{transfer-v4,
  decision-v7, transfer-v9}` (development and test). Rows land in
  `reference/out/kev/suites/` (gitignored).

  **The oracle reproduces Kev's card to the digit**, so the card's numbers
  are fp32 numbers and the comparison below is like for like:

  | | Kev's card | Kev fp32, here | fp16 bank | int8 bank (served) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | transfer-v4 dev, accuracy (656) | 0.817 | **0.8171** | 0.8155 | 0.8140 |
  | transfer-v4 dev, Brier served / raw | 0.243 / 0.269 | **0.2430 / 0.2691** | 0.2430 / 0.2691 | 0.2422 / 0.2681 |
  | transfer-v4 dev, ECE | 0.042 | **0.0416** | 0.0425 | 0.0396 |
  | transfer-v4 test, accuracy / Brier (656) | 0.838 / 0.224 | **0.8384 / 0.2242** | 0.8384 / 0.2241 | 0.8384 / 0.2238 |
  | decision-v7 dev (1,264) | 0.873 | running | **0.8726** | 0.8687 |
  | decision-v7 test (1,200) | 0.865 | – | **0.8650** | 0.8642 |
  | transfer-v9 dev, MMLU-Pro (200) | 0.565 | running | **0.565** | 0.560 |
  | transfer-v9 dev, unknowable at ≥ 0.9 (110) | 0.00 | running | 0.00 | 0.00 |

  decision-v7 dev's raw Brier on fp16, **0.2037**, is also the raw Brier
  `head.json` records for the temperature fit on those same 1,264 rows. The
  card's transfer-v9 "0.490" and "buried 0.67" are the *previous*
  checkpoint's; the current one publishes only MMLU-Pro and the unknowable
  share. (Here buried is 0.700 on both banks; transfer-v9 dev overall 0.7734
  fp16, 0.7715 int8.)

  **Row by row against Kev's fp32** (`-compare`):

  | | fp16 bank | int8 bank |
  |---|---|---|
  | transfer-v4 dev, argmax agreement | **763/764** | 761/764 |
  | transfer-v4 dev, max / mean max \\|dp\\| | 0.0030 / 0.00015 | 0.027 / 0.0024 |
  | transfer-v4 test, argmax agreement | **764/764** | 764/764 |
  | transfer-v4 test, max / mean max \\|dp\\| | 0.0011 / 0.00012 | 0.030 / 0.0023 |

  **Every disagreement is a tie in fp32**: the top two options are within
  0.001–0.002 of each other. The fp16 bank matches fp32 to about Kev's own
  isolation-gate tolerance (1e-3), and it lands on every published accuracy
  exactly or within one question.

  **What int8 costs.** It is a real quantisation, so its flips are not
  symmetric noise. Against fp16 over the four scored partitions with fp16
  controls it is **−10 questions of 4,166 (−0.24 pp)**: transfer-v4 dev −2,
  test 0, decision-v7 dev −5 (1462/1468 argmax agreement, all six flips at
  p ≈ 0.49 against 0.49), decision-v7 test −1, transfer-v9 dev −2. Calibration
  does not move (Brier within 0.001). That is smaller than the gap between
  Kev's bf16 server and its fp32 (~0.03 in p). It buys 1.2–1.4x on short
  passes (K7.1); `-kev-fp16` is the exact option and costs 3.3 GB more.

'''
s=s[:a]+new+s[b:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
grep -n 'Next: K8' CLASSIFICATION.md

Root `CLASSIFICATION.md` is the live plan (K-stages). K0–K6 and K7.1 were done on 2026-09-25: `cmd/serve -kev` serves `POST /v1/systemone`, and typesafe-sdk 0.6.0 works unchanged. The int8 bank is the default (the LLM's llm_gemm Q8 rungs; `-kev-fp16` is the control): 0.8140 on transfer-v4 dev (fp16 0.8155, Kev's fp32 0.817), 1.22–1.41x on short passes, 54 ms for the README ticket. Three Kev-owned int8 GEMMs (split-K, a wave-shared slab, register pipelining) all lost; don't retry them. K7.2 (prefix cache plus multi-pass requests, bit-identical) and K7.3 (a WMMA flash attention, 5.2x; the KV cache is fp16; branches are 64-cell aligned so isolation stays bit-exact) are done too, as is K7.4 (the GDN scan in the LLM's l8 shape, 2.3x). K7.6 fused SwiGLU into the gate+up GEMM (a Kev-owned int8 kernel with a row-block-fastest grid: llm_gemm's column-fastest order re-reads any weight over 32 MB) and chose a GEMM rung per projection. A new 2,269-token text is 761 ms, 87 ms again; the README ticket is 52 ms. K7.5 batches concurrent requests (a state slot each, 8-word row metadata, a backend worker, -kev-batch): ~29 req/s against 19.5; the naive attention is bit-exact in batches, WMMA moves answers ≤6e-4. Next: K8's fp32 check. An unexplained ≤2.5e-6 chunked-layout residue remains with WMMA; GEMM pad-row leakage and unwritten-scratch reads are ruled out by tests. `-kev` is not in ai.service yet; it would go on the small-verticals machine ([[deployment-two-machines]]).

**Why:** Jev is closed. Kev (github jaredpalmer/kev, HF jaredpalmer/kev-4b) is the open implementation: Qwen3.5-4B-Base@1001bb4d plus a rank-16 LoRA (merged) plus a pointer head, T = 2.406.

**How to apply:**
- The oracle is Kev's own code, vendored in `reference/kev/` (9fdf054) and driven by `reference/dump_kev.py` (fp32 CPU, ~3 min, 17 GB). peft 0.21.0 was added to `.venv` ([[reference-dumps-python-env]]).
- The traps: the type is `noul`; the delimiters are reused tokens (the state is fim_prefix, `<decide>` is fim_suffix, `</opt>` is box_end and is the readout); a noul's options are `[no, yes]`; the render is Python `str()` with key order preserved.
- `zimage/tokenizer.Load` now reads the pre-tokenizer regex from the file (it used to always use qwen2's, which is wrong for Qwen3.5).
- `cmd/kev -suite models/kev-suites/transfer-v4/development.jsonl` scores a suite (~40 s); build it to the scratchpad first and don't pipe it through `head` (SIGPIPE truncates its row file).
- Kill a test server by PID (`$!`), never `pkill -f` with a pattern that appears in your own command ([[watch-loops-must-not-match-themselves]]).
- `kev.ForwardRows` final-norms when every layer runs, so a per-layer comparison at the last layer is against `final`, not `layer31`.

content.text:
K8 is done: our implementation reproduces Kev-4B's published numbers. The details are under K8 in `CLASSIFICATION.md`.

**Kev's own code, run here in fp32 on the CPU, matches its model card to the digit.** On transfer-v4 dev it scores 0.8171 with Brier 0.2430 / 0.2691 (the card says 0.817, 0.243 / 0.269). On transfer-v4 test it scores 0.8384 with Brier 0.2242 (card: 0.838 / 0.224). So the card's numbers are fp32 numbers, and comparing against them is fair.

| | Kev's card | fp16 bank | int8 bank (served) |
|---|---|---|---|
| transfer-v4 dev | 0.817 | 0.8155 | 0.8140 |
| transfer-v4 test | 0.838 | 0.8384 | 0.8384 |
| decision-v7 dev | 0.873 | 0.8726 | 0.8687 |
| decision-v7 test | 0.865 | 0.8650 | 0.8642 |
| MMLU-Pro (transfer-v9 dev) | 0.565 | 0.565 | 0.560 |
| unknowable items answered at ≥ 0.9 | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 |

- **Row by row against fp32:** the fp16 bank picks the same answer on 763/764 dev questions and 764/764 test questions, with probabilities at most 0.003 apart. The int8 bank agrees on 761/764 and 764/764. Wherever an answer differs, fp32's top two options were within 0.002 of each other.
- **Cost of int8:** it is 9 questions of 4,822 below fp16 (−0.19 pp) across the five partitions with an fp16 run. That is small but not random: most of its flips go against the label. Calibration doesn't move. It still buys 1.2–1.4x speed on short passes, so I left it as the default; `-kev-fp16` gives exact accuracy for 3.3 GB more memory.
- **A card number to ignore:** the "MMLU-Pro 0.490 / buried 0.67" figures on the card belong to the previous checkpoint. The current one publishes 0.565, which fp16 hits exactly.

What changed:
- `cmd/kev` now also reports Brier (as served and raw), ECE and the unknowable share, the way Kev's scoring does.
- New `reference/kev_suite_fp32.py` produces the fp32 reference rows and resumes if interrupted.
- decision-v7, transfer-v9 and transfer-v4's test partition are copied into `models/kev-suites/`. Kev's repo was only in another session's scratchpad, so it could vanish.
- `TODO.md`, the handoff section and my memory notes are updated. I didn't commit; the auto-committer will pick it up.

**Still running:** fp32 reference runs for decision-v7 dev and transfer-v9 dev, about 4 hours of CPU in the background, writing to `reference/out/kev/suites/`. They are the two "running" cells in the K8 table. I skipped fp32 on the test partitions (about 5 more hours) because fp16 already matches the card's test numbers.

The next open item is the unexplained drift of up to 6e-4 in probabilities when requests are batched on the matrix-core attention.

content.text:
It's validating the GPU. We don't have a CPU implementation: decision D3 in the plan was not to write a Go CPU model. The CPU job is Kev's own PyTorch code running in fp32, used as the reference, and our Vulkan implementation (both banks) is what gets compared against it row by row.

Two things are being checked:
1. **That the reference is right.** Kev's fp32 run here reproduces its model card exactly on transfer-v4, so the published numbers are fp32 numbers and a fair target.
2. **That the GPU matches it question by question.** Matching the headline accuracy isn't enough on its own. The row comparison shows the fp16 bank agreeing on 763/764 and 764/764 questions, and that every disagreement is a near-tie in fp32.

The two runs still going repeat step 2 on decision-v7 dev and transfer-v9 dev, and they're worth little. Both points are already settled on transfer-v4, and the fp16 bank already hits the card's decision-v7 and MMLU-Pro numbers to the digit. What they would add is confirmation that int8's six flips on decision-v7 are also fp32 near-ties, which the fp16 comparison already shows.

I'd kill them (`kill 2429646 2428909`) and change those two table cells from "running" to "not run". Want me to do that?

Yes, sampling was enough, and nothing is running on the CPU now. The sampled runs took about 4 minutes per suite instead of the ~4 hours the full runs would have taken.

**How it was sampled:** for decision-v7 dev and transfer-v9 dev, I scored a seeded random 150 records, plus every record where the fp16 and int8 banks pick different answers (6 and 7 of them). decision-v7 also kept the 183 records the stopped full run had already written. Those deliberately chosen disagreement records make int8's agreement numbers below a worst case, not a rate.

| against Kev's fp32 | fp16 bank | int8 bank |
|---|---|---|
| decision-v7 dev, 400 questions | 399/400 agree | 395/400 |
| transfer-v9 dev, 155 questions | 155/155 agree | 148/155 |

**This corrects something I told you earlier.** I said every disagreement with fp32 was a near-tie. That holds for fp16, whose only miss here is an exact tie. It does not hold for int8. On transfer-v4 its flips were ties (margin ≤0.002), but here fp32's top-two margin on its flipped questions reaches 0.016 on decision-v7 and 0.032 on a 10-way MMLU-Pro question. They are still small, and the accuracy cost is unchanged at −0.19 pp. Three of int8's four MMLU-Pro flips land on option 8; that's too few to call a pattern.

The table and the int8 paragraph in `CLASSIFICATION.md` are corrected, along with `TODO.md`'s summary line and my memory notes. `reference/kev_suite_fp32.py` now takes `--sample N` and `--also fp16rows,q8rows` for this kind of targeted run. It also writes each record in one go, so a killed run can't leave half a record behind.

The next item in the handoff is the WMMA position residue: a request's probabilities move by up to 6e-4 depending on which other requests share its batch (and by ≤2.5e-6 across chunked layouts), only with the matrix-core attention. I'll start with the kernel.

n='''  - [x] **K7.7 — the WMMA residue was stale V** (2026-09-25). K7.3's
    ≤2.5e-6 across chunked layouts and K7.5's ≤6e-4 across batch partners
    had one cause, and it was not the layout. **A request's answers depended
    on what had run before it.** Bisected with `run` over the first L layers
    and the batch planner:
    1. Alone and batched agree when both run on a fresh device. An alone run
       after *any* batched pass is off in one row (the README ticket's
       question-2 `<decide>`), from the first attention layer on.
    2. On that row the WMMA output moves by one fp16 ulp in one element.
       Clearing **V in cells 143–191** restores it; K there, and K or V in
       a block the row sees none of (even filled with ±8192), change
       nothing.
    3. Cells 143–191 are the alignment padding after the row's own branch
       (cells 128–142), inside the 64-key block it partly sees. The row
       masks them, so P is exactly 0 there, but 0 × a stale V still moves
       the matrix cores' sum. Every segment ends in such padding, and it
       holds whatever an earlier pass wrote. The naive kernel never reads a
       masked key, which is why it was always exact.

    The fix is in `kev_attn_prep.comp`: the last row of each segment
    zeroes V from its cell to the next 64-cell boundary. The first branch
    row of a request whose state is resident (a cache hit, or a later pass
    of a long request) zeroes the state's padding. Zero is what a fresh
    device holds. It costs nothing measurable (45.0 and 27.3 ms a record,
    unbatched and batched, as before).

    **Gate passed.** transfer-v4 dev in batches of 1 and of 8 is
    **byte-identical** (was up to 6e-4 apart), and accuracy is unchanged at
    0.8140. `TestGPUBatchMatchesSingle` and `TestGPUChunkedPasses` now hold
    the WMMA kernel to the bit, as they did the naive one.
    `TestGPUStaleCacheDoesNotLeak` fills every attention layer's K and V
    with junk before cold, batched and cache-hit runs and requires the same
    bits as over a zeroed cache. Without the fix it fails by up to 2.6e-4;
    over a *zeroed* cache, batched matched alone even before the fix. All

    `TestGPUGEMMPadRowsDoNotLeak` gained the K7.6 `rb` rungs (on their own
    row-block-fastest grid) and a pad of ordinary activations. It had
    predated them, and they do not leak either.

description: "On this GPU a WMMA sum changes by an ulp when one of its zero products is -0, so a stale operand behind a +0 mask is not inert; its sign leaks."

RDNA 3.5 `coopMatMulAdd` (fp16 in, fp32 accumulate) is **not** IEEE on zero
products: `+0 * negative` = -0 in one term moves the result by ~1 ulp, while
any positive or +0 operand there is bit-exact. Magnitude does not matter; the
sign does (found 2026-09-23 through `TestGraphCheckpointIsThePrefill`, row 11
by 3.5e-4).

**Why:** the split decode attention loads whole 16-cell V tiles, so masked
cells past `n` hold stale values from a restore, rewind or earlier
conversation, and their sign leaked into the context. The fix was
`llm_attn_pack.comp` writing +0 over V cells `[n, roundUp(n, 64))`, and the

content.text:
I found and fixed the WMMA residue (now K7.7): a request's answers now come out bit-identical whether it runs alone, batched, split into several passes, or from the prefix cache. The tests pass in all four `KEV_BANK`/`KEV_ATTN` combinations.

**The cause wasn't the layout.** A request's answers depended on what had run before it on the device:
- **Symptom:** alone and batched runs agree on a fresh device, but an alone run after any batched pass was off in one row, starting at the first attention layer.
- **The stale data:** each question's branch starts on a 64-cell boundary, so the cells between the end of one segment and the next boundary are padding. That padding still holds keys and values from earlier passes. It's masked (the attention weight is exactly 0 there), but on the matrix cores 0 × a stale negative value still moves the sum by one fp16 step.
- **What rules out other explanations:** clearing the stale V there fixes it. Clearing K there, or filling a fully masked block with large values, changes nothing.
- **Why the naive attention was exact:** it never reads a masked key.

**This was already known.** My memory notes recorded the same hardware behaviour from the LLM's decode attention, and I only connected it after bisecting. I've updated the note so the next matrix-core attention starts from it.

**The fix:** `shaders/kev_attn_prep.comp` now zeroes V from the end of each segment to the next 64-cell boundary. When a state comes from the cache instead of the pass, the first question of that request zeroes the state's padding. Zero is what a fresh device holds, and the cost doesn't show in the timings.

**Verified:**
- transfer-v4 dev gives byte-identical rows in batches of 1 and of 8 (before: up to 6e-4 apart). Accuracy is still 0.8140 and speed is unchanged at 45.0 / 27.3 ms a record.
- The batched and chunked tests now require bit-identical results instead of tolerating 1e-3 and 1e-5.
- New `TestGPUStaleCacheDoesNotLeak` fills the whole KV cache with junk before cold, batched and cache-hit runs and requires the same bits as over a zeroed cache. With the fix compiled out, it fails by up to 2.6e-4.
- I also extended the GEMM pad-row test to the `rb` rungs added in K7.6, which it had never covered. They don't leak.

`CLASSIFICATION.md` (K7.7, and corrections to the K7.3 and K7.5 notes), `TODO.md` and my memory notes are updated; the diagnostic tests are deleted. The `.spv` files are gitignored, so any other machine needs a `go generate` in `shaders/` before it picks up the fix.

Nothing in the plan is known to be wrong now. The open items are the int8 bank's −0.19 pp against its 1.2–1.4x speed-up, GEMM speed, and adding `-kev` to the `ai` service.

---
name: ai-service-user-unit
description: "The ai server runs as a --user systemd unit on :11434; logs are journalctl --user -u ai, deploy.sh installs it, startup takes ~25 s, and it is deliberately served open with -token=."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
---

The `serve` binary runs as a **user** systemd unit, not a system one, and not
in the foreground:

- **Install/redeploy: `./deploy.sh`.** It builds `./ai` from `./cmd/serve`,
  substitutes the unit's `###` placeholder with `$(pwd)`, writes
  `~/.config/systemd/user/ai.service`, `daemon-reload`s and restarts.
  `./ai.service` in the repo is a *template*, not a script — running it gives
  `Permission denied`, which is the expected outcome, not a bug to fix.
- **`deploy.sh` ends with `journalctl --user -n 100 -f -u ai`,** which never
  returns. In an agent session run its steps by hand and skip the tail.
- **Logs: `journalctl --user -u ai`** (`--user` is required; it is invisible to
  the system journal). The server logs one line per backend at startup and
  `listening on http://0.0.0.0:11434` when all of them are up.
- **Startup is ~25 s** and ~13 GB peak, nearly all of it the Z-Image backend;
  tts/stt/embed land in the first 3 s. Don't conclude anything from the log
  before the image line.
- **State without tailing:**
  `systemctl --user show ai.service -p ActiveState -p SubState -p NRestarts`.
  The unit ships `Restart=always` + `RestartSec=1`, and the server `log.Fatal`s
  on any bad flag or missing checkpoint, so a config mistake becomes a silent
  ~26 s crash loop. A non-zero `NRestarts` (or "restart counter is at N" in the
  journal) is the tell; `systemctl --user reset-failed ai.service` before a
  fixed redeploy so the count reads clean.
- **Auth: omitting `-token` does not disable it.** The flag *defaults* to a
  non-empty token (`defaultToken` in `cmd/serve/main.go`), so a unit that says
  nothing about tokens requires a bearer header on every `/v1` request. Only an
  explicitly empty `-token=` opens the server. This cost an afternoon once.
- **The deployed unit runs `-token=` on purpose**, chosen 2026-09-18: open, no
  bearer header, on `0.0.0.0:11434` so the second machine can reach it. Don't
  "fix" the empty token back to a default — it is the configuration that was
  asked for. See [[deployment-two-machines]].
- The unit is **`disabled`** as of 2026-09-18 — it does not come back on boot

#!/bin/bash
set -ex

# The service file goes here:
#   ~/.config/systemd/user/ai.service
# Set it up with:
#   systemctl --user daemon-reload
#   systemctl --user enable --now ai
#   systemctl --user start ai
#   loginctl enable-linger $USER

cd "$(dirname "$0")"
go build -o ai ./cmd/serve
cat ./ai.service | sed "s|###|$(pwd)|" > ~/.config/systemd/user/ai.service
systemctl --user daemon-reload
systemctl --user restart ai.service
journalctl --user -n 100 -f -u ai

[Unit]
Description=ai
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
WorkingDirectory=###
; The LLM machine's line (research/p18-full-context.md, CONCURRENCY.md): three
; conversations at once, each with the model's whole trained context, 262 144
; cells (7.3 GB of KV cache a slot, C6). Arenas hold 8192-token batches, which
; cost decode nothing (P16); a background prefill is cut into 2048-token chunks
; so a voice command waits at most ~2 s (C3, decided over 1024). One slot is
; reserved for interactive requests (X-Priority: interactive or service_tier
; "priority"), which restore their system prompt's checkpoint (C4); unmarked
; requests are background, and concurrent decodes share a pass (C5).
; ~98 GB resident, ~68 s to come up.
;ExecStart=###/ai -addr 0.0.0.0:11434 -token= -llm -llm-ctx 262144 -llm-batch 8192 -llm-slots 3 -llm-preempt-chunk 2048 -llm-reserve 1 -llm-class background -llm-mmproj models/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GGUF/mmproj-BF16.gguf
ExecStart=###/ai -addr 0.0.0.0:11434 -token= -embed -tts -tts-gpu -stt -image -edits 3 -wyoming 0.0.0.0:10300
Restart=always
RestartSec=1

[Install]

installed unit matches template
